name: The ninety-eight latent defilements (anuśaya)
description: The root of existence: six anuśayas (passion, aversion, pride, ignorance, view, doubt), seven with passion split into sensual and existence-passion, ten with the five views; distributed by realm and by what abandons them — the seeing of each truth, or cultivation — they number ninety-eight.

equivalents.note: The seven are the base of the Kośa's ninety-eight, which are counted by realm and mode of abandonment.

name: The five (wrong) views
description: Satkāya-view (self and mine), view of extremes (permanence/annihilation), wrong view (denial of cause and result), attachment to views, attachment to rules and observances; belief in Īśvara as cause belongs to the last.

name: The four perversions (viparyāsa)
description: Taking the impermanent as permanent, the painful as pleasant, the impure as pure, and the non-self as self.

name: The outflows, floods, yokes and graspings
description: Three outflows (desire, existence, ignorance), four floods and yokes (adding views), four graspings; so named because they make beings stay, flow, carry away and hold.

equivalents.note: Kośa: three outflows (views folded in); Pali Abhidhamma: four.

name: The nine fetters (Abhidharma list)
description: Attachment, aversion, pride, ignorance, view, clinging, doubt, envy and avarice.

equivalents.note: The Abhidharma nine fetters and the Pali Abhidhamma ten share envy, avarice, pride, views, doubt, ignorance; the lists are divided differently.

name: The ten fetters (five lower, five higher)
description: Lower: satkāya-view, attachment to rules and observances, doubt, sensual desire, malice — the first three the gate, the root and the grasping; higher: passion for form, for the formless, restlessness, pride, delusion.

equivalents.note: Two different fetter lists in the same text.

name: The envelopments (paryavasthāna)
description: Eight (or ten) secondary defilements: shamelessness, lack of dread of blame, envy, avarice, restlessness, remorse, torpor, sleepiness (+ anger, concealment); for the Sautrāntika, 'envelopment' is the awakened defilement.

name: The six stains of defilement (kleśamala)
description: Deceit, dissimulation, pride, spite, enmity, harmfulness — secondary defilements traced to passion, aversion and view.

name: The five hindrances
description: Sensual desire, malice, torpor-and-sleepiness, restlessness-and-remorse, doubt; in the Kośa, belonging to the desire realm, destroying the aggregates of morality, concentration and wisdom.

equivalents.note: The Pali Abhidhamma adds ignorance as a sixth hindrance.

name: The three roots of bad (greed, hatred, delusion)
description: In the desire realm passion, aversion and delusion are the three bad roots (AK 5.20); the contemplation of the unlovely counters passion.

name: The three obstructions (āvaraṇa)
description: Obstruction of karma (the deadly acts), of defilement (intense defilement) and of ripening (bad destinies, birth in Kuru or among the non-perceiving gods), which prevent entering the path.

name: The five deadly acts (ānantarya)
description: Killing mother, father or an arhat, dividing the Saṅgha, wounding a Buddha with evil intent; they ripen in hell in the next life; the schism-lie is the gravest.

name: Schism of the Saṅgha (saṅghabheda)
description: Dividing the community by a rival teacher and path (wheel-schism) or by separate legal acts (act-schism); caused by a monk of views; its lie ripens in Avīci for an aeon.

name: Falling back (parihāṇi)
description: Loss of an attained state: for the Sarvāstivāda possible for five of the six kinds of arhat (not from stream-entry), in three forms; the Sautrāntika denies falling back from arhatship.
antidotes: perfection of the faculties (to the unshakeable lineage)

name: The four defeats (pārājika)
description: Sexual intercourse, taking what is not given, killing a human being, falsely claiming superhuman attainments — the offences that end monkhood; the Kashmiris held the fallen monk to possess both discipline and its loss.
